column3: A prior word from the Lord delaying judgment is only a broad parallel to divinely timed action.
Its exact before-and-behind horizon gives an ethical counterpart to the focus's total temporal scope.
Remembering the Lord after forgetting and submitting matters to His will speak to the focus's denial of forgetfulness.
God owns all realms and knows what is before and behind people, closely grounding the focus's comprehensive divine scope.
The honored prophets' response to recitation does not clarify commanded angelic descent or divine non-forgetting.
A command sent down by God supports the focus's claim that descent proceeds only by the Lord's command.
Its instruction to do what is commanded has only a general relation to the focus's divine command.
The immediate continuation names the Lord of heaven, earth, and what lies between, directly extending the focus's ownership claim.
The command descends between the created layers under God's encompassing knowledge, closely paralleling the focus.
Messengers come from before and behind with the call to worship God, providing a related revelation-and-horizon scene.
The inheritance of Paradise by the God-conscious does not develop descent, divine scope, or non-forgetting.
Rejection of the Quran and what precedes it offers only a limited connection to the focus's before-and-behind language.
Creation of livestock by God's hands does not illuminate the focus.
God's selection of messengers from angels and humans helps situate the angelic messengers speaking in the focus.
God knows what is before and behind people while they cannot encompass His knowledge, directly clarifying the focus's total scope.
Guards before and behind act by God's command, giving a related image of ordered protection across the same horizon.
The proud reaction to clear signs does not develop the focus's account of angelic descent.
Its retributive declaration that God forgets those who forgot the meeting directly contrasts with the focus's assurance that the Lord never forgets.
The destructive wind acts only by its Lord's command, illustrating delegated action under divine authority.
Rescue of the God-conscious and abandonment of wrongdoers does not clarify the focus.
Rain sent down from heaven is a distant instance of descent, without the focus's command or messenger theme.
Forgetting a fish in a travel narrative has no material neighbour relation.
God's knowledge of what is before and behind and the return of all affairs to Him closely echoes the focus's divine comprehensiveness.
The descent of angels on the Day of Judgment is a different descent scene with limited overlap.
The Lord's dislike of specified evils does not develop the focus.
The failed successor generation concerns prayer and desires, not the focus's reassurance about descent.
The bodily phrase between hands and feet is unrelated to the focus's temporal and spatial horizon.
Mary's wish to be forgotten is a same-surah emotional contrast but does not clarify the Lord's non-forgetting.
The selection of the most rebellious for punishment does not illuminate the focus.
A second vision at a descent has only a limited lexical link to the focus's angelic descent.
The Lord's mercy and great favor give a broad reassurance parallel to the focus's denial of abandonment.
The protected revelation cannot be reached from before or behind and is a descent from God, closely matching both motifs in the focus.
The settlement of every command offers only a general background for the focus's commanded descent.
The mention of something sent down upon angels occurs in a distinct account that does not explain the focus's descent.
Ranking people for Hell does not develop the focus's themes.
God knows what lies before and behind the angels, placing their fearful intercession within the same total divine knowledge.
God's assurance that the Prophet will not forget forms a related positive counterpoint to the focus's divine non-forgetting.
Paradisal peace and provision do not clarify commanded descent or divine non-forgetting.
Its denial that devils brought the Quran down directly distinguishes the source of the descent at issue in the focus.
God sends prophets and brings down the Book with them, supplying the broader framework for revelation governed by God.
Turning away from signs of the Lord is only a distant contrast to receiving the angelic explanation in the focus.
God brings down the Book in truth, confirming what preceded it and relating descent to a temporal scriptural horizon.
Those who forgot God are said to be forgotten by Him, a direct retributive contrast that sharpens the focus's assurance.
The gathering around Hell does not develop the focus.
The question of upon whom devils descend directly contrasts false descent with the focus's angelic descent by command.
The bee's guided paths and healing drink do not materially relate to the focus.
A decreed command in the same surah offers only a general link to action by the Lord's command.
Those who join what God commanded to be joined offer a general human counterpart to obedience to divine command.
Attentive hearing and a witnessing heart do not clarify the focus.
Jesus limits his speech to what God commanded and yields ultimate knowledge to God, paralleling the focus's obedient messenger stance.
Humanity has not yet fulfilled what God commanded, giving a limited contrast to the angels' strict obedience in the focus.
The instruction not to forget graciousness is a different human use of forgetting.
The same-surah call to worship God relates broadly to the Lordship affirmed in the focus.
The shared confession receives what was sent down from the Lord, extending the focus's revelation-from-God setting.
God sends things down only in a known measure, the closest general formulation of descent constrained by divine determination.
Those still behind in a later group use a different temporal image from the focus's total before-and-behind scope.
God's retributive forgetting of people who forgot the Last Day directly contrasts with the focus's declaration that the Lord does not forget.
Angels are sent down only with the truth, directly paralleling the focus's restriction of angelic descent to God's command.
The opening mention of mercy to Zachariah does not develop the focus's themes.
Paradisal lodging and reward do not clarify the focus.
The continuity of messages to earlier messengers is only a broad background for the focus's revelation setting.
Preservation of believers' reward does not materially relate to divine non-forgetting or descent.
Revelation sent down to both communities provides a related transmission context under the Lord's authority.
What lies before and behind an event defines its exemplary warning, a limited temporal parallel to the focus's encompassing horizon.
Comfort and provision given to Mary do not clarify the focus.
A chosen messenger is guarded before and behind, closely linking controlled revelation transmission with the focus's horizon language.
The Lord does not destroy towns before sending a messenger, supporting the focus's assurance of ordered, non-neglectful divine dealing.
Barriers before and behind form an inverse image of the focus's all-encompassing scope, showing a horizon closed to people.
The prohibition on taking angels as lords clarifies their subordinate status under the Lord whose command governs their descent.
The explicit assurance that the Lord has neither forsaken nor detested the Prophet closely parallels the focus's denial of abandonment.
The angel identifies himself as a messenger of Mary's Lord, a same-surah instance of angelic service under divine authority.
God sends angels down with the Spirit from His command, directly matching the focus's central claim.
Creation of heaven, earth, and what lies between them supports the focus's claim that the intervening realm belongs to God.
The one Lord and resulting worship offer a concise theological continuation of the Lordship asserted in the focus.
The question about who sends down rain has only a general descent link.
No messenger brings a sign except by God's permission, closely supporting the focus's restriction of angelic action to command.
The inviolability of the Book is related to revelation but does not clarify the focus's descent or non-forgetting.
The calf story's statement that Moses forgot uses forgetting in an unrelated narrative sense.
False companions beautify what is before and behind people, an adverse counterpart to the focus's claim that every horizon belongs to God.
Circulation between Hell and boiling water does not illuminate the focus.
Rain awaited before being sent down is only a distant temporal-descent parallel.
God communicates only by prescribed modes, including sending a messenger who reveals by His permission, closely framing the focus's message.
Revelation as inspired communication broadly supports the focus's account of an angelic message under command.
Rain and God's sudden command form a distant instance of descent and divine timing.
The visible sky and earth before and behind people give a concrete spatial counterpart to the focus's encompassing horizon.
The challenge to false partners does not develop the focus.
A woman's command and coercive threat are unrelated to divine command or descent.
The Prophet is commanded to uphold revelation sent down by God and justice, a broad parallel to divinely ordered communication.
God as creator and guide offers only a general grounding for the focus's Lordship.
The Book's descent from God directly supports the focus's revelation-and-descent setting.
The certainty of the Lord's punishment does not clarify commanded descent or non-forgetting.
Those distributing an affair provide a limited image of agents executing a commanded order.
The oath by the earth and its spread does not develop the focus.
Defiance of the Lord's command and messengers is a broad negative counterpart to the obedient descent in the focus.
The barrier between people and their desires does not clarify the focus's horizon language.
The accusation of hastening the Lord's command offers only a limited connection to divinely timed action.
Marriage restrictions and the call to Paradise do not relate to the focus.
The hypothetical descent of an angel-messenger is explicitly conditioned by the recipients' nature, illuminating purposeful divine dispatch.
The division of believers for learning and warning does not clarify the focus.
Each heaven receives its own command, extending the focus's vision of divine order across the heavens.
Gabriel brings the Quran down upon the Prophet by God's permission, directly matching descent governed by the Lord's command.
The Lord reinforces believers with angels sent down, a concrete instance of purposeful angelic descent.
God sends down the revelation with His knowledge and the angels bear witness, joining descent to comprehensive divine knowledge.
The demand for an angel to be sent down, and its refused timing, forms a close counterpoint to the focus's explanation of controlled descent.
God declares that He will forget those who forgot the meeting with Him, directly contrasting the focus's assurance that the Lord never forgets.
God answers believers by reinforcing them with a succession of angels, showing angelic dispatch as a divine response.
God's sending down and preserving the Reminder closely supports the focus's assurance that revelation is neither neglected nor forgotten.
The angels fear their Lord above them and do what they are commanded, directly explaining the obedient agency voiced in the focus.
The Spirit is described as being from the command of the Lord, closely connecting the angelic messenger to the focus's governing command.
The revelation comes down from the Creator of earth and the high heavens, placing descent within the Lord's cosmic authority.
To God belongs what is in the heavens and earth and what lies between them, almost exactly restating the focus's ownership claim.
Moses states that his Lord neither errs nor forgets, the Quran's closest explicit parallel to the focus's final assurance.
One who forgot God's signs is in turn forgotten on the Day of Judgment, clarifying the deliberate contrast with God's own non-forgetting.
The angels are honored servants rather than independent actors, directly supporting their subordinate role in the focus.
The angels do not precede God in speech and act only by His command, a near-exact explanation of the focus's first clause.
The objection that no angel was sent down with the Messenger directly frames the question answered by the focus's account of angelic descent.
The Quran is sent down in a measured way to strengthen the Prophet, clarifying that delayed or staged descent has divine purpose.
God directs the affair from heaven to earth, giving a close cosmic counterpart to the focus's command-governed descent.
The Spirit is revealed to the Prophet by God's command, directly aligning revelation, the Spirit, and divine command.
The angels do not disobey what God commands and do exactly what they are ordered, directly corroborating the speakers' obedience.
The angels and the Spirit ascend to God, complementing the focus's descent scene with their return toward the same Lord.
God declares that He has sent the Quran down gradually, directly supporting the focus's purposeful, non-neglectful timing of revelation.
The Quran's descent on the Night of Decree supplies a concentrated statement of revelation arriving at an appointed divine time.
The angels and the Spirit descend by permission of their Lord with every affair, the closest explicit parallel to the focus's claim.
